edition.locus: Gebhardt VII.VI (Hilarianus; ad bestias; the weaning)

source_text: Alio die cum pranderemus, subito rapti sumus ut audiremur. Et peruenimus ad forum. Rumor statim per uicinas fori partes cucurrit, et factus est populus immensus. Ascendimus in catastam. Interrogati ceteri confessi sunt. Uentum est et ad me. Et apparuit pater ilico cum filio meo, et extraxit me de gradu dicens: Supplica; miserere infanti. Et Hilarianus procurator, qui tunc loco proconsulis Minuci Timiniani defuncti ius gladii acceperat: Parce, inquit, canis patris tui, parce infantiae pueri. Fac sacrum pro salute imperatorum. Et ego respondi: Non facio. Hilarianus: Christiana es? inquit. Et ego respondi: Christiana sum. Et cum staret pater ad me deiciendam, iussus est ab Hilariano proici, et uirga percussus est. Et doluit mihi casus patris mei, quasi ego fuissem percussa: sic dolui pro senecta eius misera. Tunc nos uniuersos pronuntiat et damnat ad bestias; et hilares descendimus ad carcerem. Tunc quia consueuerat a me infans mammas accipere et mecum in carcere manere, statim mitto ad patrem Pomponium diaconum, postulans infantem. Sed pater dare noluit. Et quomodo deus uoluit, neque ille amplius mammas desiderat, neque mihi feruorem fecerunt, ne sollicitudine infantis et dolore mammarum macerarer.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: on another day while they were eating lunch they were suddenly seized for a hearing and brought to the forum, a rumor ran through the nearby parts and a huge crowd gathered; they went up onto the platform, the others when questioned confessed, then her turn came; her father at once appeared with her son and dragged her down a step begging her to offer sacrifice and pity the child; Hilarianus the procurator, then holding the sword-right in place of the dead proconsul Minucius Timinianus, urged her to spare her father's grey hairs and the boy's infancy and to sacrifice for the emperors' welfare; she refused, declared herself Christian, saw her father beaten with a rod by Hilarianus's order when he persisted, grieved for his wretched old age as if struck herself; then Hilarianus pronounced all of them condemned to the beasts and they went down to prison joyful; since the baby used to nurse from her and stay with her in prison she sent the deacon Pomponius to her father to ask for the child, the father refused, and by God's will the child no longer craved the breast nor did her breasts inflame, so she was not worn out by anxiety for the child and pain in the breasts.
pass_b_english: Another day, while we were at lunch, we were suddenly hurried off to be heard, and we came to the forum. At once a rumor raced through the quarters around the forum, and an immense crowd formed. We went up onto the platform. The others, when questioned, confessed. My turn too came. And immediately my father appeared with my son, and he pulled me down from the step, saying, Offer the sacrifice; have pity on the child. And Hilarianus the procurator, who had then received the power of the sword in place of the dead proconsul Minucius Timinianus, said, Spare your father's grey hairs, spare the infancy of the boy. Perform the rite for the welfare of the emperors. And I answered, I will not do it. Hilarianus said, Are you a Christian? And I answered, I am a Christian. And while my father stood there to cast me down, he was ordered by Hilarianus to be thrown out, and he was beaten with a rod. And my father's fall pained me, as if I myself had been beaten: so I grieved for his wretched old age. Then he pronounces us all and condemns us to the beasts, and in joy we went down to the prison.

Then, because the child had been accustomed to take the breast from me and to remain with me in the prison, at once I send Pomponius the deacon to my father, asking for the child. But my father would not give him. And as God willed it, the child no longer craved the breast, nor did my breasts become inflamed, so that I should not be worn away by anxiety for the child and by pain in the breasts.

lemmas.gloss: seized to be given a hearing
from the step of the platform
offer sacrifice, perform the act of supplication
the power of the sword, capital jurisdiction
he pronounces sentence and condemns to the beasts
I was worn away, wasted by distress

choices.why: dative of interest with parce; canis here means white hairs of age, appealing to pity for old age, parallel to infantiae pueri
impersonal passive ventum est marks sequence in the interrogation after ceteri; renders the procedural turn, not physical motion
rejected: it was come even to me

choices.why: quomodo with indicative gives attendant circumstance for the double relief that follows, not manner of wanting
